<div class="section-heading">
# July Analyst X Data Science Huddle
</div>
Recently, we had our July Analyst X Data Science Huddle!

We heard from two projects:

* Discrete Event Simulation (DES) model to support ADHD and Autism pathway analysis presented by Guled Abdullahi
* Optimising Access to OCT in the Diabetic Eye Screening Digital Surveillance Pathway presented by Simon Wellesley-Miller

As always, thank you to our presenters for sharing their interesting work!

Missed the session? [Check out the recording and PowerPoint slides here](https://future.nhs.uk/DataAnalytics/view?objectID=56936784){target="_blank"}, where you will also find the recordings of previous huddles.

___

<div class="section-heading">
# September Analyst X Data Science Huddle
</div>
**Tuesday 8th September 2026, 13:30 - 14:00, Online**

The Data Science Community for Health and Care have organised the next Analyst X Data Science Huddle for September. We will hear from one project; see the abstract below.

* **Synthesis: Turning Video Content into Searchable Institutional Memory Presented by Eirini Komninou**

Your team watches hours of webinars, conference talks, and recorded meetings - then that knowledge disappears. Synthesis is a privacy-first pipeline that automatically turns video and audio into a structured, cross-linked, searchable knowledge base, stored on your own infrastructure. This huddle will be presented by Eirini from the Strategy Unit.

<div class="section-heading">
# Events
</div>
Lots of exciting things coming up! See the [full calendar here](https://future.nhs.uk/DataAnalytics/view?objectID=861745){target="_blank"}, and a small selection below.

### [London Data Week](https://londondataweek.org/ldw26-events/){target="_blank"}
**4 July 2026 - 12 July 2026, Various Times, Various Locations**

London Data Week (LDW) is a citywide, week-long public festival of data. Different organisations across London design and host public events over the week of the festival. 

Take a look at the link for all the London Data Week events on this year!

### [Whose AI is it anyway? Data, sovereignty, and the geopolitics of intelligence](https://www.lse.ac.uk/dsi/events/2025-26/public-events/whose-ai-is-it-anyway){target="_blank"}
**Wednesday 8 July 2026, 18:30pm - 20:30pm, Bush House, King's College London, 30 Aldwych, WC2B 4BG**

In-person public event hosted by the Data Science Institute and King's Institute for Artificial Intelligence as part of London Data Week.

When Anthropic's Fable 5 was ordered offline worldwide just three days after its release, it sharpened a question artificial intelligence increasingly raises: who's in control?

​Most governments talk about 'sovereign' AI and some are now building it, but what does it really mean for a country, an institution, or a citizen to have a say over those systems? What happens when that control slips?

​Join the LSE Data Science Institute and [King's Institute for Artificial Intelligence](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/ai){target=} for a public panel bringing together leading voices to explore the technology, politics and security of AI and data sovereignty, and what's at stake for the UK.

Followed by a drinks reception.

### [BriCS x Turing - Isambard-AI workshop (21st July 2026)](https://www.turing.ac.uk/events/brics-x-turing-isambard-ai-workshop-21st-july-2026){target="_blank"}
**Tuesday 21 July 2026, 10:00 - 16:00, Enigma 2.0, The Alan Turing Institute, British Library, 96 Euston Rd, London, NW1 2DB**

The Bristol Centre for Supercomputing (BriCS) and The Alan Turing Institute are running a joint 1-day introductory workshop on Isambard-AI.

The workshop is open to participants from UK research organisations (e.g. universities, NHS bodies, research institutes) and industry (UK registered business of any size with a Companies House registration number).

The workshop is free but you must register for a place. The workshop covers:

* Introduction to Isambard-AI 
* Distributed PyTorch Training  
* PyTorch Profiling 
* Containers
